key_insight: OpenGEM26 enables a graph neural network force field, GPTFF-mol, that learns diverse organic molecular energetics and forces from large optimization trajectories rather than only equilibrium structures.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a faster surrogate for DFT-based molecular simulation, supporting efficient screening and dynamics of sulfur- and chlorine-containing organic molecules.
method: Built OpenGEM26 with 200,000 unique molecules and 4.4 million conformations containing H, C, N, O, S, and Cl.
Computed structures and trajectories at ωB97X-D/Def2-SVP and Def2-TZVP levels with dispersion corrections.
Trained a graph neural network potential (GPTFF-mol) on equilibrium and non-equilibrium geometries to predict energies and forces.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an energy MAE of 16 meV/molecule (0.82 meV/atom) and improved force prediction versus ANI-2x, with validation on butane rotation and keto-enol tautomerization.
watch_item: Performance may depend on coverage of the training chemistry and size range, so extrapolation to larger or more diverse molecules could require caution.
paper_title: Graph Neural Network Force Fields (GPTFF-mol) for Organic Molecules from Optimization Trajectories (OpenGEM26)
